title: Maintaining agent instructions
description: How to keep AGENTS.md and related files short, true and useful.

rules.title: Keep the root file short
rules.text: Keep the root agent file to always-on rules and pointers. Put detail in the document that owns the topic.

rules.title: Nested files per package
rules.text: Add nested AGENTS.md files for packages with their own commands or rules, and read the nearest one before editing there.

rules.title: Link, do not copy
rules.text: Link to the authoritative config or doc instead of copying versions, rule lists and counts that go stale.

rules.title: Verified commands
rules.text: List only commands that work from a clean checkout, with the working directory they expect.

rules.title: Thin tool entry files
rules.text: Keep CLAUDE.md and other tool-specific entry files as thin pointers to AGENTS.md.

rules.title: Directory map
rules.text: Include a short map of directories and what lives where, so an agent can find the right place without searching.

rules.title: Commands never to run
rules.text: State commands an agent must never run, such as long-running dev servers or destructive scripts, and mirror them in tool permission lists.

rules.title: Encode repeated corrections
rules.text: Turn a correction you repeat into a lint rule, test or script. Keep the instruction file for what tooling cannot enforce.

rules.title: Suggest updates
rules.text: Suggest an update to the agent file when you learn something durable about the project that it is missing.

rules.title: Point to skills
rules.text: Point to reusable skills for repeatable workflows and name the task each one covers.

rules.title: Dedicated review guide
rules.text: Point review agents to a review guide so authoring and review follow the same conventions.

rules.title: Remove stale pointers
rules.text: Remove a pointer and its document together when a topic disappears.

rules.title: Path-scoped guidance
rules.text: Say which guidance applies to which paths, so agents load backend, frontend and test rules only when relevant.
